content: The search strategy included terms related to interventions, evaluations, assessments, and various study designs. These terms were used to identify relevant studies in databases such as PubMed, CINAHL, and Embase. Specific terms included intervention, evaluation studies, program evaluation, randomized controlled trial, controlled clinical trial, randomized, clinical trials, non-randomized trial, pre-post study, before-after study, time series study, cross-sectional, double-blind procedure, single-blind procedure, retrospective cohort, and trial. Studies involving animals were excluded unless they also included human data. The search also focused on self-efficacy, self-concept, empowerment, self-esteem, self-perception, decision-making, power, and risk reduction behaviors. These terms were used to identify studies addressing these psychological and behavioral factors. After removing duplicates, 1,938 records were screened at the abstract level, and 145 abstracts were reviewed. From these, 72 full-text articles were assessed, and 20 studies evaluating 10 interventions were included in the review. Articles were excluded if they did not meet inclusion criteria, resulting in 52 exclusions at the full-text level. The systematic review aimed to identify interventions that facilitate safe disclosure of HIV status for women living with HIV who fear or experience violence. The review included articles from databases such as PubMed, CINAHL, and Embase, with a cut-off date of April 1, 2015. Secondary reference searching and expert consultations were conducted to identify additional relevant studies. Conference abstracts from major HIV and violence-related conferences were also reviewed. Search terms included combinations of disclosure, violence, abuse, rape, forced sex, coerced sex, HIV, and AIDS. For the question on modes of delivery for women living with HIV, the review examined maternal and perinatal outcomes associated with different delivery methods. Databases searched included PubMed, CINAHL, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, with a cut-off date of October 1, 2015. Search terms included HIV, AIDS, mode of delivery, cesarean section, and C-section. A total of 1,750 records were identified, with 64 full-text articles assessed for eligibility. Thirty-six articles were included in the review, with two reporting on randomized controlled trials and 34 on observational studies. Articles were excluded for reasons such as lack of stratification by delivery mode, abstracts only, combined elective and non-elective C-sections, hypothetical models, duplicate data, and outcomes not of interest. For the question on medical and surgical abortion outcomes among women living with HIV, the review compared these outcomes to those of HIV-uninfected women. Databases searched included PubMed, CINAHL, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, with a cut-off date of April 1, 2015. Search terms included abortion, induced, abortion, therapeutic, termination of pregnancy, menstrual regulation, HIV, and AIDS. Conference abstracts and grey literature were also reviewed. Full-text articles were assessed for eligibility, and relevant studies were included in the review.
